Getting Started#

The cemd package revolves around the AtomicSystem class, which serves as the primary container for all atomic data: coordinates, topology, box parameters, masses, and force field parameters.

Loading a System#

The easiest way to load a system is directly from a LAMMPS .data file:

from cemd import AtomicSystem

system = AtomicSystem.from_file("waterbox.data")
print(system)

Other supported formats include .cif and .pdb:

system = AtomicSystem.from_file("structure.cif")
system = AtomicSystem.from_file("molecule.pdb")

Inspecting a System#

Once loaded, the AtomicSystem object provides immediate access to physical properties and topology:

# Basic properties
print(f"Box parameters [a, b, c, α, β, γ] : {system.box}")
print(f"Number of atoms : {system.num_atoms}")
print(f"Atom types      : {system.atom_types}")
print(f"Density         : {system.density:.3f} g/cm³")
print(f"Total charge    : {system.total_charge:.4f} e")
print(f"Volume          : {system.volume:.2f} Å³")

Saving a System#

To write a system back to a LAMMPS .data file:

# Save with the default atom style (preserved from the input file)
system.write("output.data")

# Specify the atom style explicitly
system.write("output.data", atom_style="full")    # full: id mol type charge x y z
system.write("output.data", atom_style="charge")  # charge: id type charge x y z

Note

The .data format is the recommended output format for LAMMPS simulations. The system can also be exported to the .pdb.

Converting a System#

Another solution to save to other formats is to convert the AtomicSystem to a MDAnalysis Universe. The MDAnalysis package allow to write in many formats.

u = system.to_mda()
print(u)

<Universe with 2709 atoms>

struct = system.to_pmg()
print(struct)

Explore structure databases#

You can explore the COD and PubChem open databases to find structures and load them in an interactive way.

Visualization#

You can visualize your system in VMD directly from Python :

# Static view of the current configuration
system.view()

# View with an associated MD trajectory
system.view(trajectory="md_production.dcd")

Next Steps#

  • Build new systems with the cemd.builders module.

  • Compute structural and dynamic properties with the cemd.analysis module.

  • Apply force field topology with set_topology().
